policy_notes.note: HUD 2026 Budget Management Letter: vouchers are funding-constrained. PHAs asked to stop issuing new vouchers (except HUD-VASH and FYI), pause new project-based voucher commitments, and cut payment standards, ending exception payment standards and staying inside the 90-110% basic range. Expect payment standards toward the low end of the range.
NSPIRE inspections for vouchers delayed to 2027-02-01 (third extension). Until then PHAs may still inspect under the old HQS (24 CFR 982.401). The checklist here aims at both.

Emergency Housing Vouchers are ending: families under EHV HAP contracts on 2026-09-30 move to Tenant Protection Vouchers by 2026-12-31 (PIH 2026-25); closeout from early 2027. For a landlord the lease continues as an ordinary voucher.
PHAs may use HCV admin fees for landlord signing/retention bonuses, security and utility deposits and holding fees (PIH 2022-18). Optional and per PHA; 2026 budget pressure makes them scarcer.

Columbus Metropolitan Housing Authority (CMHA, cmhanet.com): HCV payment standards (SAFMR by ZIP) - cut to 100% from 110% effective 2026-08-01 (100% of SAFMR by ZIP (was 110%); effective 2026-08-01 for new leases/moves/new HAP contracts). ZIP table PDF is a scanned image (no text layer); only metro FMR page read. Existing leases keep old standard until lease term ends.

local_programs.name: CMHA HCV landlord onboarding
local_programs.landlord_gets: HAP after contract; inspection within 1-10 days of RTA; quarterly landlord class. No bonus/damage fund found. Payment standards reduced to 100% SAFMR for new contracts from 2026-08-01 due to HUD funding shortfall.

reasons: City permit/licence required: Yes: annual STR permit from the Building & Zoning Services License Section for dwellings with 5 or fewer guestrooms rented under 30 days; notarized application and fingerprint BCI checks for applicant, host, 24-hour contact and manager; one permit per dwelling.
Caps/density: No numeric cap on permits or nights in Ch. 598; permits can be denied or revoked after 3+ calls for service in 12 months or a nuisance history.
Pending: Zone In: the new 2024 Zoning Code (Title 34) was adopted July 2024 and applies in phases to rezoned parcels; parcels not yet rezoned stay under Title 33.

permit.value: Yes: annual STR permit from the Building & Zoning Services License Section for dwellings with 5 or fewer guestrooms rented under 30 days; notarized application and fingerprint BCI checks for applicant, host, 24-hour contact and manager; one permit per dwelling.

primary_residence.value: No. Host must be the owner or a 'permanent occupant' (lives there 51%+ of the year); non-resident owners can hold permits. Tenants need written landlord consent to STR use.

zones.value: Ch. 598 has no zone list; a permit does not authorize STR use where other law prohibits it, and the city tells applicants to confirm zoning first.

caps.value: No numeric cap on permits or nights in Ch. 598; permits can be denied or revoked after 3+ calls for service in 12 months or a nuisance history.

max_occupancy.value: No STR-specific guest cap in Ch. 598; an STR is limited to dwellings with 5 or fewer guestrooms; housing-code space limits apply.

taxes.value: City hotel/motel/STR excise tax totals 5.1% (Ch. 371) on stays under 30 days; county and other lodging taxes not checked.

listing_id.value: Yes: permit number must appear on every platform listing; platforms may not book without it; permit displayed in the unit; host and platform keep records 4 years.

pending.value: Zone In: the new 2024 Zoning Code (Title 34) was adopted July 2024 and applies in phases to rezoned parcels; parcels not yet rezoned stay under Title 33.

state_preemption.value: No statewide STR preemption enacted. HB 563 (134th GA, 2022) was reported from committee but never passed; later bills not checked.
